title: a) Interest rate swap contracts which generallyentail the contractual exchange of fixed and floating interest
columns:
Notes (continued)
33 Derivative assets and derivative liabilities (continued)
33.1 Use and measurement of derivative instruments (continued)
Swaps are transactions in which two parties exchange cash flows on a specified notional amount for a
predetermined period.
The major types of swap transactions undertaken by the Bank are as follows:
a) Interest rate swap contracts which generallyentail the contractual exchange of fixed and floating interest
payments in a single currency, based on a notional amount and an interest reference rate.
